description: The sources disagree on whether barrier damage increases zinc uptake from zinc oxide. SCCS reports no damaged-versus-healthy difference, including UVB-damaged pig skin in vitro. Pal 2016 reports that UVB enhanced zinc oxide nanoparticle penetration in hairless mice. Ågren 1991 shows much higher systemic zinc through full-thickness rat wounds than through intact human skin. Yasugi 2026 attributes an infant's hyperzincemia to absorption through eroded diaper dermatitis. The models differ in species, damage type, vehicle and measure.
value_a_verbatim: UVB damaged skin did not enhance the penetration of Zn (pig, in vitro)
value_b_verbatim: UVB exposure enhanced the dermal penetration of zinc oxide nanoparticles (SKH-1 mouse, in vivo)
resolution_or_reason: Not resolvable from this package. Both findings are kept with their models. No single statement about 'damaged skin' is drawn. The wound, eroded-dermatitis and UVB models are reported separately.
